items.claim: Keep the stackless original error in the stack-fallback test. Change the guard in `GraphQLError.js:195` from `if (originalError && originalError.stack)` to `if (originalError)`. The merge-base test fails with `expected undefined to be a string`; the head test still passes.
items.consequence: `creates new stack if original error has no stack` now passes `new Error('original')`, which has a stack, so it takes the same branch as the previous test. Nothing tests the `Error.captureStackTrace` fallback any more, and a GraphQLError wrapping a stackless error could end up with `stack === undefined` unnoticed.
items.proposed_fix: In `src/error/__tests__/GraphQLError-test.js`, build the stackless original explicitly: `const original: any = new Error('original'); original.stack = undefined;`, keeping the other assertions. In a scratch copy this passes on the real code and fails on the mutant.
